The *Sakuṇajātaka* (Ja 36), translated in English as *The Bird*, is a birth-story belonging to the Pali *Jātaka* collection. According to the narrative framework recorded in the tradition, the story was delivered by the Buddha while staying at Jetavana, occasioned by a monk whose monastic cell had burned down. The narrative opens in translation with the verse line "Ye denizens of air".

None of the references in the examined secondary literature discuss this specific text, instead referring to other bird-related stories such as the *Tesakuṇajātaka* (Ja 521) or *Javasakuṇajātaka* (Ja 308).
